column1: # The 6 ayah numbering systems, with the count each one reports.
# The six systems already have dictionary entries — they are the values of the
# `ayah_numbering_system` classification, and those entries say what each one
# is. This registry carries what an entry should not: the numbers.
# A total is a fact with a chain behind it, not a constant. Al-Dani reports each
# school's total on the authority of a named transmitter, and reports the rival
# figures beside it — the Basrans are given as 6204, and also as 6210 and 6216
# from other transmitters on the same page. `total` is the figure al-Dani gives
# as that school's own count; `also_reported` is what else he reports for it.
# Software that prints one number without the other is printing an opinion.
# `qiraat` lists the readings conventionally paired with the school. The pairing
# is conventional: a numbering school and a reading are different things that
# travelled together, and neither one derives the other.
# NOT HERE YET: the per-surah counts. Al-Dani gives every surah its own section
# naming its count in each school and every disputed boundary — that is the
# dataset an application actually needs, and 114 sections of spelled-out Arabic
# numerals is an extraction job, not a transcription. Until it is done and
# checked, this file carries the totals only, and the gap is stated rather than
# filled with a table from somewhere else.
# The codes are the ones the dictionary already uses for these six systems.
# The keys used by quranpedia/qiraat-ayah-map (madani-first, madani-last, kufi,
# makki, basri, dimashqi) are carried as alternative spellings, so a dataset
# keyed either way resolves to the same system.
# `ref` cites al-Bayan fi Add Ay al-Quran, volume/page.
# code
ayah_numbering_madani_awwal
ayah_numbering_madani_akhir
ayah_numbering_makki
ayah_numbering_kufi
